metadata.scope: I-beams, H-beams, U-channels, T-sections, RHS, CHS, aluminium extrusions, and roof/bridge trusses.

material_suggestions.use_case: welded structural I-beams, channels, and angles
material_suggestions.notes: Yield 235/275 MPa; cut, weld, and prime.
Anodised finish; slot for T-nuts; good corrosion resistance.
Use for brackets and end-caps only, not load-bearing beams.

material_suggestions.material: A36 / S275 structural steel tube or flat bar
material_suggestions.use_case: welded or bolted roof and bridge truss members
material_suggestions.notes: High load capacity; add gusset plates at nodes and check buckling in compression members.

material_suggestions.use_case: architectural roof trusses and timber king/queen-post frames
material_suggestions.notes: Use bolted steel plates or timber joinery at nodes; allow larger member depth than steel.

material_suggestions.use_case: lightweight removable trusses, display rigs, and machine guarding
material_suggestions.notes: Lower stiffness than steel; increase section depth and avoid slender compression members.

standards_used.name: EN 10034 I and H sections
standards_used.note: IPE 100: height 100 mm, flange 55 mm, web 4.1 mm, flange 5.7 mm.

standards_used.name: 2020 aluminium extrusion (OpenBuilds)
standards_used.note: 20×20 mm section; 6 mm slot; M5 T-nut head 5.85×2.75 mm.

standards_used.name: Queen-post truss geometry
standards_used.note: Rise/span ratio 0.3–0.5; queen posts at span/4 from centre; straining beam at queen post tops.

standards_used.name: Truss member layout practice
standards_used.applies_to: roof and bridge truss node/member geometry
standards_used.note: Members connect node-to-node; panel_length = span/panel_count; gusset plates are placed at chord and web intersections.

standards_used.name: AISC / Eurocode truss design assumptions
standards_used.applies_to: steel truss proportions and member checks
standards_used.note: Compression members require buckling checks; tension members require net-section and connection checks.

output_policy.openscad_code: Geometry-only OpenSCAD with named parameters, one module, and no prose.

parts.name: Parametric I-beam (flanges + web)

fit_guidance_mm.end_connection: drilled bolt holes or welded end plate

design_rules: THREE cubes in union — NOT one solid rectangle
top flange at Z = beam_height/2 - flange_thickness/2
bottom flange at Z = -(beam_height/2 - flange_thickness/2)
web centered at Z=0 with height = beam_height - 2*flange_thickness
a single cube([beam_length, flange_width, beam_height]) is WRONG
validation_criteria: three cube() calls in union for flanges and web
flange at ±beam_height/2 positions
web height = beam_height - 2*flange_thickness
failure_modes: single solid rectangular block — functionally wrong I-beam
web and flanges merged into one box — not parametric
missing web — just two plates

constraint_checks.expression: three cube() in union for flanges+web
constraint_checks.message: I-beam MUST be three cubes: top flange, bottom flange, and web. A single cube is a rectangular bar, not an I-beam.

constraint_checks.expression: no single cube spanning full beam_height
constraint_checks.message: Do not use a single solid bar as an I-beam.

parts.name: Standard tapered-flange I-beam / S-shape
main_features: flanges thicker near web than at outer edges
design_rules: Use this when prompt says standard I-beam, classic I-beam, S-beam, or tapered flange.
Do not model as wide H beam.
Use tapered flange polygons or hull approximations, not constant wide flanges.
Expose beam_height, flange_width, flange_thickness_outer, flange_thickness_inner, web_thickness, beam_length.
validation_criteria: top and bottom flanges exist
central web exists
flange_width < 0.70 * beam_height
tapered flange thickness is represented or named
failure_modes: using wide H-beam proportions
using a single rectangular block
missing flange taper

parts.name: Narrow-flange I-beam / IPE-like section
design_rules: Use this when prompt says narrow flange, IPE, or slim I-beam.
Flanges are parallel and narrow, not tapered.
Model with three rectangular prisms.
validation_criteria: three solids: top flange, bottom flange, web
flange_width < 0.70 * beam_height
web centered between flanges
failure_modes: wide H-beam proportions
single rectangular bar

parts.name: Wide-flange H-beam / W-beam / HEA-style section

flange_thickness.note: often thicker than narrow IPE flange

design_rules: Use this when prompt says H-beam, wide flange, W-beam, HEA, HEB, or universal column.
Flange width should be close to beam height.
Do not use narrow I-beam proportions.
validation_criteria: three solids: top flange, bottom flange, web
flange_width >= 0.75 * beam_height
web centered between flanges
failure_modes: using narrow IPE proportions for an H beam
single rectangular bar

parts.name: Common truss features, parameters, formulas, and OpenSCAD helpers

main_parameters.truss_width: side spacing or plate thickness direction
main_parameters.truss_type: king, queen, Pratt, Howe, Warren, Fink, K, etc.

non_main_parameters.gusset_radius: visual node plate radius or half-width
non_main_parameters.bolt_diameter: bolt or hole diameter at gussets/supports
non_main_parameters.support_pad_length: bearing plate length at each support
non_main_parameters.support_pad_width: bearing plate width at each support
non_main_parameters.member_clearance: small visual clearance between overlapping plates if needed
non_main_parameters.node_plate_offset: offset for front/back gusset plates in double-sided trusses

gusset_thickness_rule.formula: 0.25 to 0.40 * member_width for visual CAD models

assumptions: The truss is represented as pin-jointed straight members for geometry generation.
Members meet at shared node coordinates; loads are assumed to be applied at nodes.
OpenSCAD output is conceptual CAD geometry and not a certified structural calculation.
Compression members require buckling checks; tension members require net-section and connection checks.
Gusset plates and bolts are visual/mechanical features unless detailed fastener sizing is requested.
material_suggestions: A36/S275 steel flat bar or RHS for heavy welded/bolted trusses
6061-T6 or 6082-T6 aluminum tube for lightweight frames and display trusses
Glulam or C24 timber for roof trusses
PETG/PLA/PA-CF only for prototypes, teaching models, and non-load-bearing parts
parts.usage: Shared reference for generating any real-world truss with chords, web members, nodes, gussets, bolts, supports, and parameter formulas.
design_rules: Use member_between(p1,p2) for each physical member.
Use arrays or loops for repeated panel points.
Keep formulas visible as named variables when possible.
Show connection features at nodes when user asks for realistic truss details.
Do not generate a single solid triangular slab for a truss.
validation_criteria: continuous bottom chord exists
top chord/rafters exist
web members connect at common nodes
major nodes have gusset plates when realistic detail is requested
supports are placed at +/- span/2
named formulas exist for panel_length and diagonal/rafter length
failure_modes: flat triangle with no separate members
members floating without shared node intersections
no bottom chord
wrong diagonal direction for Pratt or Howe prompts
missing gusset/bolt/support details in realistic requests

parts.name: King-post roof truss

rise.formula: 0.25 to 0.40 * span for pitched roof trusses

depth.formula: span/8 to span/12 for bridge-style trusses

panel_count.note: even count preferred for symmetric web layouts

assumptions: Straight prismatic members joined at ideal pin-like nodes.
Loads assumed to enter at nodes for conceptual geometry generation.
OpenSCAD output is CAD geometry, not certified structural analysis.
Compression members require buckling checks outside the CAD model.
material_suggestions: A36/S275 steel flat bar or RHS
C24 timber or glulam
6061-T6 or 6082-T6 aluminum tube
PETG/PLA/PA-CF only for scale models or unloaded prototypes
parts.usage: Short-span roofs, sheds, porches, and small timber/steel frames.
main_features: one central vertical king post from bottom chord to apex
two angled struts from bottom-center joint to midpoint nodes on the rafters
design_rules: Use endpoint-based member_between(p1,p2) placement for every member.
Do not model a truss as one filled triangular plate.
For king-post trusses, split rafters at the strut-to-rafter nodes so the visible joints are left support to left strut node to apex to right strut node to right support.
For king-post trusses, do not add a horizontal straining beam or collar beam unless explicitly requested.
Keep named parameters for span, rise/depth, panel_count, member size, gusset size, and bolt diameter.
Place gusset plates at nodes where members meet.
validation_criteria: separate visible members between node points
continuous bottom chord
rafters segmented through both strut-to-rafter nodes
correct web-member direction for requested truss type
gusset plates/node plates present when realistic detail is requested
support pads at left and right bearings
failure_modes: single triangle or solid plate instead of member assembly
missing bottom chord
missing angled struts from bottom-center joint to rafters
one long rafter hides or skips the strut-to-rafter joint
horizontal straining beam added to a default king-post truss
diagonals in the wrong direction for named truss type
members not meeting at common nodes
no gusset plates on realistic bolted/welded truss requests
